# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [1.0.0-beta.8] - 2026-10-18

### Added

- **Wallpaper Editor: View › Show Debug › Show Hitboxes**, as Wallpaper Engine's editor has it: every visible Puppet Warp image's hit boxes, one per bone in the bone's colour, posed as the scene plays. A cursor event's `hitBox` names the bone whose box is under it; a bone that moves no vertex has a 1-unit box, which shows as a dot. The setting is kept between windows.
- **Particles: a layer image emitter's "update emission bitmap periodically" and "inherit layer motion"** (`layerimage` flags 0x20000 and 0x40000), as Wallpaper Engine 2.8 runs them. With the first, the emitter samples its layer again once a second while it emits, from the picture the layer shows then (a video's frame, a texture animation's frame, a texture a script set), on the GPU without holding up the frame, and keeps emitting from the old points until the new ones are in. With the second, a particle launches with its point's motion since the last time it emitted, times a share between the emitter's `speedmin` and `speedmax` (0.1 and 0.2 by default). On a Puppet Warp layer the points now follow the rig: each takes the bone whose hit box holds it, as Wallpaper Engine assigns them, and particles spawn where that bone has moved its part of the picture.
- **Puppet Warp blend rules**, as Wallpaper Engine plays them. A bone with a blend rule (Edit Constraints › Blend Rules) is pulled toward its target bone by the weight its clip keys: its position, rotation and scale move toward the target's, its children follow, and bone physics then acts on the result. A rig whose rule was deleted keeps still, as in Wallpaper Engine.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Puppet Warp: blend rules**, as Wallpaper Engine's Edit Constraints › Blend Rules. In the Skeleton tool the selected bone's **Blend Rules** section adds a rule toward another bone or deletes one; in the Animate tool each rule's weight (0 to 1) is keyed at the current frame of the animation, and Add Key and Delete Key include it. The preview pulls the bone as the wallpaper will, and rules made in Wallpaper Engine open and save back.
- **Puppet Warp clipping masks**, Wallpaper Engine's Puppet Warp › Clipping Masks. A limb assigned to a mask is drawn only where the mask, painted over other limbs, covers it; **Invert mask** shows it only away from them; nested masks intersect; **Additive blending** adds the limb to what's under it; **Hide mask geometry** hides the painted-over limbs, which still mask. As in Wallpaper Engine, the clipping shows with materials drawn by `genericimage4`; the editor's default puppet material (`genericimage2`) draws the limb whole, keeping the masks' draw order and hidden limbs. The editor's stats count the clipping mask passes.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Puppet Warp › Clipping Masks**, Wallpaper Engine's panel. Pick a limb (an island of the mesh) on the canvas or in the list and **Assign Clipping Mask** (a new mask, named, or one another limb has), then **Paint Clipping Mask** over the limbs it may show over (Draw or Erase, size, hardness, opacity); **Remove Clipping Mask**, **Additive blending**, the mask's **Name**, **Invert mask** and **Hide mask geometry** as in Wallpaper Engine. The masks are saved in the puppet's `.mdl` as Wallpaper Engine's editor writes them, and a puppet made in Wallpaper Engine keeps its masks (and their names, from its editor file) when it's edited and saved, where they used to be dropped.
- **Wallpaper Editor › texture variants**, Wallpaper Engine 2.6's Texture Properties › Variants. An image layer's inspector has a **Variants** section: **Add Variant Group**, and in each group **Add Option** (an image, or a video for a video texture, of the texture's size and kind; anything else gets Wallpaper Engine's "Incompatible Variant Option"), each option with its picture, Rename Option, Replace Texture, Remove Option, its order (the first option whose condition holds wins), **Replace** or **Alpha blended** (uncompressed RGBA 8888 textures only) and its **Condition**: a checkbox, or a combo with one of its values, an existing property or a new one (a new combo gets a Default for the base and one value per option). **Preview** switches the bound properties so the canvas shows an option. As in Wallpaper Engine, only a texture imported with the editor takes variants. Every change writes the texture again as Wallpaper Engine's resource compiler does (laid out as its own file, checked against a Wallpaper Engine capture: the `.tex` with its option records and per-mipmap patches, beside it the `.tex-json` in Wallpaper Engine's shape) into the edits, one undo step, and the player composes it as Wallpaper Engine's loader does.
- **Puppet Warp inverse kinematics**, as Wallpaper Engine plays it. A bone with the "Inverse kinematics arm/leg" constraint now reaches for its IK target while an animation plays: the limbs above it bend toward the target, on the side of the orientation controller, and lie straight toward it when it is out of reach; with **Rotate when overstretched** the end bone turns to point at the target over the **Full rotation distance**, otherwise it keeps the target's orientation. Bone constraints that limit an IK limb's angle and the target's bend rules apply too. Puppets without IK draw exactly as before.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Puppet Warp: kinematic chains**, as Wallpaper Engine's Edit Constraints › Physics. A bone's **Simulation mode** is Not simulated, Spring physics, Rigid physics or **Kinematic chain**, with the presets Inverse kinematics arm/leg and Rope with 4 elements, Limb depth and Behavior; Inverse kinematics has Use orientation controller, Rotate when overstretched and Full rotation distance, Rope has Gravity enabled, Stretch enabled, Free endpoint, Mass and Friction. In the Animate tool the chain's IK target (◆) and orientation controller (●) are dragged on the canvas to key them, Add Key and Delete Key include them, and the preview solves the chain as the wallpaper will. Chains made in Wallpaper Engine open and save back.
- **Puppet Warp rope chains** ("Rope with N elements"), as Wallpaper Engine simulates them while an animation plays: the chain hangs under the scene's gravity with the bone's mass, pinned at its root and, unless **Free endpoint** is on, at its end, swinging and settling, and the scene's wind (Physics › Wind) blows it about. **Stretch enabled** lets it stretch to reach a target further than its length.

### Changed

- **Scene Edit / Export opens faster.** Each effect file's shaders are read once per open instead of once per layer, Wallpaper Engine's labels are loaded once instead of once per layer, and a layer's JSON is parsed once per edit instead of on every redraw. On a 276-effect scene the window's model is ready in about 240 ms instead of 1.8 s, on a 123-effect scene in about 200 ms instead of 800 ms.
- **Video length and size checks read only the boxes they need.** Finding a video texture's length (SceneScript's video duration) and a movie's picture size (the Wallpaper Editor's movie import and texture variants) no longer copy the whole movie into memory first: on a 218 MB video each check allocated 218 MB and took 10–50 ms, and now allocates nothing and takes under 0.1 ms. Both walk the movie's box headers with the sample entry repair's `MP4Box`.
- **Particles always simulate on the GPU.** The CPU particle simulation, which ran only when the GPU one couldn't be made (and as the tests' reference), is gone. If the GPU simulation can't be made, the error is logged and no particle system draws; the rest of the scene still does.
- **Cleanup:** unused Wallpaper Editor code (a texture variant check, a shader editor diagnostics list, a second copy of the character sheet packing) and an unused "Create a Playlist" string are gone.
- **Wallpaper Editor: imported models are compiled as Wallpaper Engine 2.8 compiles them**, checked against WE 2.8.0.42's own import of a rigged FBX (capture 546) and its recompiles of three default-project models. An imported model's `models/<name>.json` now has WE's shape: `skinning`, and under `editor` the animations' ids (`animationmapping`), clips naming their animation, `motionflags` as WE stores them, attachments as a transform and each bone's constraint with WE's whole key set; configurations the editor wrote before are still read. Animations get the ids the configuration gives them, a clip's record carries WE's flags and empty mode, a static mesh in a rigged model is bound to its own node, bones are in WE's order and their bind pose, and bone constraints are compiled as WE compiles them (one angle limit on every simulated axis, the tip, the largest offset). Animations are turned into tracks as WE turns them (its keys, linear in between, on whole frames, the last frame looping to the first), meshes share a polygon's corners, every texture coordinate set takes part in joining vertices, and tangents have WE 2.8's handedness. Add Clip names the clip and sets root motion as WE's does. WE's recompiled `bars.obj` and `flow.obj` now come out the same, and `pistols.fbx` with the same vertices, its triangles in another order (docs/model-import.md).
- **Normal Map Generation** is checked against Wallpaper Engine 2.8's own output for the same picture and settings, pixel by pixel (a permanent test); the map was already Wallpaper Engine's to well under a step on average.

### Fixed

- **Wallpaper Editor: Add Effect's previews show what the effect does.** A built-in effect is set on the test card as Wallpaper Engine's own preview of it sets it (the `preview` project in the effect's folder: its values, held to their sliders' ranges, its combos and its masks), so Shake moves the card sideways with Wallpaper Engine's direction map, and Skew, Transform, Chromatic Aberration, Opacity and others no longer look like the plain card. Effect previews render again (cache revision 3).
- **A scene's first complete frame waits for its volumetric light shafts.** The volumetrics' pipelines compile in the background like the others, but the renderer didn't count them, so a frame it called complete (what the screen saver, Live Photos and depth captures start from) could lack the shafts.
- **A scene's first complete frame also waits for its shadows and its puppets' texture channels.** The shadow casters' and the texture channels' pipelines compile in the background too and weren't counted either, so a complete frame could have casters missing from the shadow atlas or a puppet without its channels. A model pipeline that lands while a frame is drawn now also keeps that frame from counting as complete.
- **Workshop: card previews seen a moment ago show at once again.** Their thumbnails were kept in a cache the system could empty whenever it wanted memory, so a card could flash its placeholder and download its preview again; they now stay (most recently used first, up to the same 96 MB) and are dropped only under critical memory pressure.
- **Scene Edit / Export: Save in a JSON editor tells you when the text isn't a JSON object.** Saving an object, material or particle whose edited JSON doesn't parse (or isn't an object in braces) used to do nothing without a word; it now shows a Couldn't Save alert with the parser's reason, and nothing is saved. A scene, model, material, particle or package file that is there but can't be read or decoded when Scene Edit / Export or the properties panel opens is now logged (one line each) instead of silently showing as missing.
- **Saved library, Workshop and app state that can't be read or written is logged.** Playlists, display wallpapers, recent wallpapers, the Workshop and Steam player caches, conversion manifests, Workshop preset projects, the crash relaunch record and macOS's shortcut list used to fall back without a trace when they didn't decode or save; each failure is now one error line in the log (Import, Library, Workshop or App), with the same fallback. A missing file stays quiet.
- **Wallpaper Editor: reads and decodes that fail are logged.** Scene edits that can't be applied or digested, a model's companion files, configuration or additional animation files that can't be read, New Wallpaper templates that don't parse, a project.json the property editor can't read, the depth map plug-in's state and a GPU depth map pass that falls back to the CPU used to fall back silently; each failure is now one error line in the log (category Editor), with the same fallback. The app's Log Level applies to it.
- **Wallpaper Editor, web and audio reads that fail are logged.** A wallpaper file, added asset or Wallpaper Engine asset the editor finds but can't read, its project.json, timeline index and Puppet Warp sources, a texture variant that can't be scaled, the depth map editor's scene, a stored Chromium finding or engine manifest that doesn't decode, and a movie whose tracks can't be read for its audio level used to fall back silently; each failure is now one error line in the log, with the same fallback.
- **Scene sound on an output device at another sample rate no longer allocates memory on the audio thread.** When the default output device runs at a rate other than the one the scene's sound engine was made at, the output resamples through Core Audio's converter, set up as before and driven so the realtime callback allocates nothing (it made 7 to 8 heap allocations per callback before; the audio thread must never wait on the allocator). The sound is sample-for-sample the same.
- **Wallpaper Editor: Escape cancels a timeline drag.** Pressing Escape while dragging keyframes or a curve handle drops the drag: the keyframes go back where they were, the rest of the drag does nothing and nothing is added to Undo. Escape without a drag still clears the keyframe selection.
- **Wallpaper Editor: the script and timeline panels' heights** are kept in the app's own defaults, like every other setting, so a test run or an isolated development copy no longer writes them into the user's real preferences.
- **Development and CI assets: Wallpaper Engine's New Wallpaper templates and script editor snippets.** `Scripts/fill-assets-cache.sh` keeps `projects/templates` (as `templates`) and `ui/dist/monaco/snippets/*.js` (as `snippets`), as the app's assets cache does, and `Scripts/fetch-we-assets.sh` downloads both, so the asset-gated tests of the New Wallpaper wizard and the script editor's snippets run on CI. The CI asset cache's key carries a revision, bumped for the new files.
- **MCP: `owe-mcp` reaches an isolated copy of the app** (`OWE_ISOLATED_STATE=<tag>`, a development or test copy) again. The copy's control socket no longer depends on its support folder or temporary folder: it is `/private/tmp/owe-<uid>/isolated-<hash of the tag>.sock` for the copy and for every `owe-mcp` given the same tag, in an owner-only folder both sides check is really the user's own. The user's own app keeps its socket where it was.
- **Wallpaper Editor: binding a texture to a Texture or User Shortcut property** now writes the link where Wallpaper Engine's editor does, into the layer's material (its first pass's `usertextures`, one entry per texture slot, any slot), not into the scene object; a layer whose material is shared with another keeps the old form, and drafts saved with it still read. New properties are numbered as Wallpaper Engine numbers them in project.json (`index` their place without the scheme colour, `order` 100 + `index`), and a new property's key is made from its title as Wallpaper Engine makes it ("Custom texture" is `customtexture`: lower case, without spaces or punctuation).
- **Wallpaper Editor: importing an image with Crop transparent area** keeps the picture where it was in the full frame, as Wallpaper Engine does: the layer is placed by the crop's offset and the model records it as `cropoffset`, which Align with Background then uses.
- **Wallpaper Editor: Character Sheet Creation** puts the new sheet layer at the scene's centre, as Wallpaper Engine does, instead of where the old layer was.
- **Text with an opaque background at partial opacity** now fades as in Wallpaper Engine: the box shows through the faded glyphs instead of being covered by them, and `backgroundbrightness` is read (it scales the box where Wallpaper Engine applies brightness). Letter spacing, the box's size and padding and its bloom were checked against Wallpaper Engine 2.8 and already matched.
- **Clicking a 3D model** hits the whole model again: the hit box is the mesh's bounds, so a model around its origin is clicked in every quarter, not only above and right of its origin (Wallpaper Engine 2.8's own behaviour, checked against it). `localPosition` is where the click meets the box, from its centre in model units.
- **A scene with "clear" turned off** (`general.clearenabled` false) starts on black, as in Wallpaper Engine, instead of its clear colour, which nothing then clears it to.
- **`Scripts/scene-api-coverage.py` runs again.** It read a file the scripting runtime left long ago; it now takes the object model from the typings fixture the runtime is tested against and `engine`/`input` from the runtime's JavaScript, stops with an error when a source it needs is missing, and doesn't count a script's own fields (`thisScene.world = …`) as missing APIs.

## [1.0.0-beta.7] - 2026-10-16

### Added

- **Wallpaper Editor: a View menu**, as Wallpaper Engine's editor has it. **Reset Camera** fits the scene in the canvas again; **Show Desktop Preview** frames what a display of the **Preview Aspect Ratio** (4 : 3, 16 : 10, 16 : 9 or 21 : 9) shows of the scene and **Show Phone Preview** what an upright phone shows, dimming the rest and hiding the handles while it is on; **Show Grid** draws a grid on the scene; **Show Selection Box** turns the selected layer's outline off or on; **Show Debug** › **Show Particle Collision** draws the particle systems' collision planes, spheres and rectangles, and **Show Particle Control Points** their control points; and **Low FPS Simulation** runs the canvas at Wallpaper Engine's 22 frames per second, to see how the wallpaper behaves on a slow computer. The grid, previews and Low FPS Simulation are also buttons beside the canvas's zoom, and the settings are kept between windows.
- **Wallpaper Editor: multiple selection and Wallpaper Engine's context menu commands.** Shift- or ⌘-click adds a layer to the selection on the canvas or in the layer list, dragging from an empty place on the canvas selects the layers the marquee touches, and Option-click picks the layer under the selected one where several are stacked. Dragging, the arrow keys, Delete and Duplicate act on every selected layer, each as one undo step. A layer's context menu adds **Center**, **Align with Background** (an image Wallpaper Engine cropped on import, back where it was on the full picture), **Rotate CW** and **Rotate CCW**, **Copy Transforms** and **Paste Transforms**, **Move to Custom Position…** and **Copy All Effects** and **Paste All Effects**; an effect's menu adds **Copy Effect**, **Paste Effect**, **Paste Effect Settings** (onto the same effect) and **Duplicate Effect**, as in Wallpaper Engine's editor.
- **Wallpaper Editor: effect gizmos**, as Wallpaper Engine's editor draws them from an effect's `gizmos`. While an effect is open in the inspector, its handles show on the layer and drag its settings, each drag one undo step: the four corners of Perspective (and of Clouds, Reflection, Cursor Ripple and Light Shafts in perspective), the centre, size and ellipse of Spin and Twirl, the hinge, centre and page of Swing, and the point and line emitters of Advanced Fluid Simulation with their size and direction (shown only for the emitters its settings turn on). A setting the shader marks as a position (Spin's centre, say) is a point on the canvas and X and Y in the inspector; one marked as a direction is a dial, in degrees where Wallpaper Engine shows degrees. A setting a user property sets is shown but not dragged.
- **Wallpaper Editor: gizmo modes and a 3D gizmo**, as Wallpaper Engine's editor has them in the canvas's upper left corner. **Translate** shows arrows that move the selection along x or y (or freely from the centre), **Rotate** a ring that turns it (Shift: 15° steps), **Scale** a handle per axis of the layer and a centre that scales it evenly, and **Multi** (2D scenes) every handle together, as before; clicking the active mode again hides the handles. **World Space** and **Local Space** choose whether Translate's and Rotate's handles follow the scene's axes or the layer's own, each mode keeping its choice (Translate starts in World Space, Rotate in Local Space). A 3D scene's layers are no longer edited in the inspector only: it opens in Translate, the gizmo sits on the selected object as the scene's camera shows it, with arrows, rings and scale handles along x, y and z, and clicking near an object's origin selects it. Each drag is one undo step and is drawn live.
- **New Wallpaper…** (the library's Add Wallpaper menu), Wallpaper Engine's editor welcome page and template wizard. **From a Picture** makes a scene the picture fills, with its title and scheme colour (the picture's dominant colour to start); a picture that isn't a display size gets WE's advice and **Resize Picture** to one of WE's sizes in the picture's shape (Widescreen, Ultra Widescreen, Dual and Triple Monitor, Portrait), the largest it fills recommended, scaled to cover it and cropped to the centre; a portrait picture is warned about. **From a Template** makes WE's Empty scene at a size, or a copy of one of the 2D scene templates of your Wallpaper Engine copy (`projects/templates`, which the assets cache now keeps) with each picture it asks for replaced, the scene sized to it when the template says so. **Import Folder** makes a web wallpaper of a folder with an `index.html`, or imports a wallpaper's folder as it is. New wallpapers go into the Wallpaper Storage folder with a preview, and a new scene opens in the Wallpaper Editor.
- **Stats overlay**, Wallpaper Engine's "Stats per frame". The Wallpaper Editor's toolbar has **Show Stats** (Never, Auto, Always; Auto, the default, shows only the numbers past Wallpaper Engine's limits): over the canvas, FPS, GPU time, active texture memory (red past 400 MB), dynamic lights (past 6), script execution time (past 10 ms), expensive and very expensive effects (effect.json `performance`; red past 10 and 1), draw calls, primitives drawn, shader programs (past 100), framebuffer copies, particle count, memory and simulation time (past 10 ms), render target changes (past 100), video textures (past 3) and clipping mask passes. Scene Edit / Export shows a compact readout of FPS, GPU time and texture memory under its preview, red when any number is past its limit. The renderer counts only while a readout is on screen, and then draws every frame, idle or not, so the numbers are a frame's; otherwise its frames run exactly as before.
- **Wallpaper Editor: the script editor's Snippets and Edit menus, Run / Stop Preview and the console's options**, as in Wallpaper Engine's editor. **Snippets** has Insert Function (every callback, documented for the field's type), Insert Property (Slider, Checkbox, Text, Color, Combo, added to the script's `createScriptProperties()` chain or a new one after the imports), Import Base Module (Color, Math and Vector Utilities), Import Custom Module (the other modules of WE's `scripts/jsmodules`) and **Replace Script** with WE's snippets: Rainbow Color, Flicker, Drag & Drop, Click Play Sound, Rotation, Rotation Pivot, Screen Bounce, Audio Factor, plus Click Wiggle, Cursor Avoid and Cursor Follow. WE's own snippet scripts are read from your Wallpaper Engine copy (`ui/dist/monaco/snippets`; the assets cache now keeps a copy), and the editor's own versions stand in where WE has none. **Edit** has Format Document (re-indents by brackets and method chains), Comment Selection (⌘/), Uncomment Selection (⌥⌘/) and the SceneScript documentation. **Stop Preview** stops the canvas's scripts (every field back to its authored value) and **Run Preview** starts them again from the beginning, noted in the console. The console has **Clear Log on Run** and **Auto Scroll**, kept between sessions. A script property declared with `new Vec3(…)` (WE's colour form) now shows in the script's properties.
- **Wallpaper Editor: Texture, User Shortcut and Group properties, a folder's fetch mode and a file's type**, the types Wallpaper Engine's editor creates that it couldn't. A **Texture** (`scenetexture`) or **User Shortcut** (`usershortcut`) property starts unset, as WE writes them, and lists the layers whose texture follows it, with **Bind to Layer**: the layer's albedo is linked in its `instance.usertextures`, by the key for a texture and as `{"name", "type": "usershortcut"}` for a shortcut (whose icon the layer then shows; scripts open it with `engine.openUserShortcut`). Renaming the property re-points the links. A **Group** folds the properties after it, up to the next group, in the preview as in Wallpaper Engine's sidebar, and the list indents its members. A **Folder** has WE's **Fetch Mode** (On Demand, the default, or All: `mode` `ondemand` or `fetchall`), and a **File** its **File Type** (any, image or video: `fileType`). The MCP `add_user_property` takes the new kinds too.
- **Wallpaper Editor › sound layer properties**, as Wallpaper Engine's: a sound layer's inspector lists its samples and edits the mode (Loop, Random, Single), the volume, the random mode's minimum and maximum time, Mute in Editor, Start Silent, and Spatialization with its attenuation start distance and attenuation. Each change is one undo step in the draft; a volume a user property sets shows which one.
- **Wallpaper Editor › image layer properties**, as Wallpaper Engine's inspector groups them: Parallax Depth in the transform (while the scene's camera parallax is on, for a layer without a parent), Brightness in Appearance, a Miscellaneous section (Perspective Rendering, Enable Click Events, Disable Click Propagation, Copy Background for composition and fullscreen layers, Alignment), Texture › Clamp UVs, and **Lighting & Reflections** for layers drawn with WE's generic image shaders: Lighting and Reflection, the normal map and the material's roughness, metallic, specular tint, emissive colour and brightness and reflectivity. Lighting & Reflections edits the layer's material as WE's editor does; the edited material is kept with the draft (never written into the wallpaper), read by the scene in place of the file and written into a copy saved with Save as New Wallpaper. Each change is one undo step.
- **Texture user property** (Wallpaper Engine's `scenetexture`, "Bind User Property" on a layer's texture). A wallpaper that offers one shows a file row in Details: the picture (PNG, JPEG…) or video (MP4, MOV) you pick replaces the layer's image, drawn at the size the author's image had, and a video plays. With nothing picked the layer keeps its own image. Picking or clearing a file reloads only that layer.
- **Texture variants** (Wallpaper Engine 2.6's Texture Properties › Variants). A texture that carries variant options swaps or blends them in as the wallpaper's user properties choose: a checkbox turns its option on, a combo picks one option per variant group, and an unused value shows the base texture. **Replace** options replace their part of the image (RGBA, RG88, R8 and DXT1/3/5 textures) or the whole image or video, **Alpha-blended** ones are drawn over the base by their own alpha, as Wallpaper Engine composes them when it loads the texture; changing the property reloads only the layers that use it. These textures used to fail to load, since their option records were read as a video flag.
- **HDR videos in HDR** on the Metal video path, as Wallpaper Engine 2.8's "Scene DX11 (HDR Support)" video framework. With Post-Processing set to Ultra (Display HDR), a PQ (HDR10) or HLG video wallpaper decodes as linear light in half floats and reaches the display as EDR, finished by Wallpaper Engine's `combine_video_hdr`: highlights above SDR white show above it, clamped at 2 × (headroom − 1) times SDR white as Wallpaper Engine clamps them. SDR videos, and every video under the other settings, play on the 8-bit path as before, at the same cost. The AVKit path already showed HDR video as EDR.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Add Layer › Model: Import FBX or OBJ…**, as Wallpaper Engine's Add Asset › Model takes a model file. The file is imported (its model, materials and textures kept with the edits) and added as a model layer; an FBX or OBJ dropped on the canvas or the asset browser is imported the same way, at the drop point in a 2D scene. The model picker lists the models imported this way under **Imported**, between the wallpaper's own and Wallpaper Engine's. A texture the model names that isn't beside it is reported, and the material draws white until one is chosen.
- **Wallpaper Editor: the Model Editor** (a model layer's **Configure Model…**, for models imported from FBX or OBJ), Wallpaper Engine's tabs: **Animation** (the model's animations with **Add Clip**, **Add FBX File…** for more animations of the same skeleton, and each clip's start and end frame, frame offset, frame rate, loop, mirror or single playback, Match loop and root motion with its bone and axes; a clip or animation can be played on the layer), **Attachments** (named points on bones, with origin and angles), **Events** (named frames of an animation or clip, which scripts receive as `animationEvent`) and **Constraints** (each bone's physics with Puppet Warp's presets, spring or rigid, per-axis rotation and position, gravity, copy and paste). A **Materials** tab does what WE's Advanced Texture Settings does on the model's materials: the shader (Generic, Foliage, Fur, Chroma), its options (lighting, reflection, rim lighting, toon shading, tint mask, fog…), its textures (albedo, normal map, the PBR map's metallic, roughness, reflection and emissive channels…) and its values, all read from the shader. OK compiles the model again and points every layer drawing it at the new one, one undo step. WE 2.8's Blend Layers and Transitions tabs are switched off in WE itself, so they aren't here. Clean Project now keeps an imported model's materials, configuration and sources.
- **Wallpaper Editor: FBX and OBJ model import**, as Wallpaper Engine 2.3 and later import models. A model file is compiled into Wallpaper Engine's `.mdl` the way WE's resource compiler writes one: polygons triangulated, normals, tangents and texture coordinates as WE's importer gives them, identical corners joined, a static model's parts merged per material, and for a rigged FBX its bones (with the nodes above them), skin weights and every animation sampled at the file's frame rate. The source, its configuration (WE's `models/<name>.json` keys: normals, tangent space, a second UV set, clips, events, attachments, bone constraints), the model and a `generic4` material per mesh material with its texture are kept with the edits. Against the models in WE's default projects, whose sources ship beside the compiled files, 27 of their 34 meshes come out with WE's format, vertices and triangles (7 byte for byte, the rest within 0.0002 in their floats); the other 7 differ in which near-equal corners are joined (docs/model-import.md). FBX and OBJ are read with the bundled ufbx library (v0.23.1, MIT); Collada, glTF, .blend, .3ds and .lxo, which WE's Assimp also reads, aren't.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Scene Options and Project Settings**, as Wallpaper Engine's. With nothing selected, the inspector edits the scene's settings in WE's groups: General (background, ambient and sky reflection colours, transparent object sorting), Bloom (on/off, strength, threshold, tint, and Ultra post-processing (HDR) with its strength, threshold, smoothing, scatter and iterations), Camera (FOV, near and far Z, zoom, camera shake and camera parallax with their settings), Distance Fog, Height Fog and Physics (gravity direction and strength, wind on/off, direction and speed). Project Settings edits the title (Save as New Wallpaper suggests it; File › Save writes it into a wallpaper of your own) and the scene's resolution. Each change is one undo step in the draft; a setting a user property sets shows which one. Camera parallax turned on by hand is no longer turned off again by the depth-parallax rule.
- **Wallpaper Editor: Character Sheet Creation**, as Wallpaper Engine's (Image Editing in an image layer's context menu). Split a cut-out character into limbs in WE's hierarchy (the Body, then limbs under limbs, each added by name), each limb separated with the Foreground Separation tools from what its parent, or the limb before it, leaves. OK lays WE's pieces out on one texture, each cut to its opaque pixels with WE's spacing and arranged into a square, replaces the layer with it as `<texture>_sheet` in one undo step, and opens Puppet Warp on the sheet ([docs/image-tools.md](docs/image-tools.md#character-sheet-creation)).
- **Wallpaper Editor: Foreground Separation**, as Wallpaper Engine's (an image layer's context menu, Image Editing). Mark the foreground and background with WE's brush, or outline it with its polygon tool, tune it with WE's Fine-tuning (Fill gaps, Mask tolerance, Smoothing, Quality level), and check it with its View buttons (Original, Foreground & Original, Foreground, Background, the mask with M). The brush's marks go through GrabCut, as in WE's editor, which finds the outline from rough strokes; where WE starts from the strokes alone, macOS's Vision finds the objects in front first, on the Mac, so a picture is already separated before anything is drawn. OK replaces the layer's picture with the background, the separated area filled from around it, and adds the foreground as a new layer just above it, in one undo step ([docs/image-tools.md](docs/image-tools.md#foreground-separation)).
- **Wallpaper Editor: Normal Map Generation**, as Wallpaper Engine's. An image layer's inspector has a Normal Map section with **Generate…** and **Remove**. Generate opens WE's generator with its options and defaults (Shape: Blur 63, Depth 1, Exponent 4, Threshold 1; Details: Blur 21, Depth 1, Invert) and a preview of the map beside the picture; it builds the map as WE's editor does, a rounded shape from the picture's outline (its distance inside and outside) and details from its brightness, turned onto the shape. OK writes it as WE names it (`<texture>_normal`, imported as WE's `rg88n` normal map) and makes it the layer's normal map in one undo step, turning Lighting on when neither Lighting nor Reflection is, since WE draws a normal map only with one of them. The wallpaper's files are never changed: the layer uses a copy of its material kept with the editor's files ([docs/image-tools.md](docs/image-tools.md)).
- **Wallpaper Editor: an editable effect's Shader Options**, as Wallpaper Engine's material properties: each of its materials' **Blending** (Normal, Translucent, Additive, Alpha to coverage), **Culling** (No cull, Normal), **Depth test** and **Depth write** (available, as in WE, only for normal or alpha-to-coverage blending with the depth test on). A change rewrites the effect's material in the edits as WE writes it, one undo step, and the canvas draws with it.
- **Wallpaper Editor: the Shader Editor**, as Wallpaper Engine's. An editable effect (My Effects) lists its **Shaders** in the inspector, each with **Edit**, which opens it docked under the canvas: WE's shader dialect highlighted (keywords, types, `texSample2D`/`mul`/`CAST3` and GLSL's functions, the engine's `g_*` constants and `a_*` attributes, preprocessor lines, annotations) and completed (⌥⎋ or F5: the dialect's words, WE's headers' functions and constants, the shader's own names). **Snippets** has WE's menus: Replace Shader (WE's basic and masked effect shaders, read from your WE copy), Add Include (`common.h`, `common_blending.h`, `common_fragment.h`, `common_vertex.h`), Add Constant (General, View, Texture Sampler with the next free `g_Texture<n>` up to WE's 10, Texture Info, Audio) and Add Variable (Slider Float and Int, Linked Sliders, Color Picker, UV Position Picker, Knob, and the three combos), each written where WE writes it with WE's annotation. **Apply** (⌘↩) or **OK** writes the shader into the edits (one undo step) and the canvas rebuilds it ("Rebuilding shaders"); the app's translator checks the pair as the scene loader translates it, puts each error on its line of the file you edit (past the prelude, the inlined includes and the front end's edits) and, as in WE, **View Errors** shows the text the failing step compiled with the error's line marked. The effect's controls follow the edited annotations at once.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Add Effect: New, Duplicate and My Effects**, as in Wallpaper Engine. **New** makes an editable effect from Wallpaper Engine's blank effect (read from your copy of its assets) and **Duplicate** copies the selected one, built-in or the wallpaper's, both under a name you choose (WE's folder name: `Pulse+` becomes `effects/pulse_`); the new effect is added to the layer. Its `effect.json`, material and shaders are written as Wallpaper Engine writes them (a one-material effect's material and shader renamed after it, group `localeffects`, `editable`), and kept with the edits: undoable, in the draft, written by File › Save and into a wallpaper saved with Save as New Wallpaper. **My Effects** lists them first, with the wallpaper's own editable effects; **Delete** removes one made in the editor (layers using it keep it, as in WE).
- **Letter spacing on text layers** (Wallpaper Engine 2.8's `spacing`). Its first number is added to every character's advance and its second to the line height, in the same units as the text's layout, as Wallpaper Engine lays text out; wrapping at `maxwidth` counts it. 3802509485 authors 10.48 for both.
- **Text layer backgrounds** (Wallpaper Engine's `opaquebackground` and `backgroundcolor`, the editor's *Background*). The text's block, its lines plus the padding, is filled with the colour behind the glyphs (and behind outlines, blur and shadows), whether the wallpaper turns it on or a script does (`thisLayer.opaquebackground`, `thisLayer.backgroundcolor`). Layer opacity and brightness apply to the box as to the text.
- **Wallpaper Editor: Wallpaper Engine's project tools.** The asset browser lists the project's files in WE's folders (Textures, **Materials**, Models, **Particles**, Sounds, Fonts) and has a Project menu: **New Material…** (WE's "Enter filename for the new material:", a `materials/<name>.json` kept with the edits), **Clean Project…** (the editor's files that neither the draft, the saved edits nor any file they use names, listed for checking, then moved to the Trash) and **Clean Local Storage** (what the wallpaper's SceneScripts stored in `localStorage`; the canvas's scripts start again from nothing). An image layer's context menu has **Edit with External Image Editor**: its picture opens as a PNG in the app you choose (asked the first time, or with **Choose External Image Editor…**), and each save there is imported again as the layer's image, one undo step each.
- **Wallpaper Editor: Wallpaper Engine's image importer options.** Adding images (Image…, the asset browser's Import, or a drop) asks first, as WE's importer does: the texture **format** (High Quality RGBA 8888, the default, Good Performance DXT5, High Performance DXT1, or the uncompressed RG 88 and R 8 channels), **Pixel Art Optimization** (no bilinear filtering), **No Mip Maps**, **Clamp UVs** (on by default), **Crop transparent area** with a padding (the layer is the cropped size) and a **normal map**, imported beside the image as its material's second texture (`<texture>_normal`, RG 88 as WE's `rg88n`). With WE's defaults a PNG or JPEG is still kept as it is; any other choice writes a `.tex` laid out as WE 2.8's importer writes one (a `TEXB0004` of raw texels, DXT padded to 32-pixel tiles, LZ4 where it is smaller, mipmaps halving while the smaller side stays at 64 or more). An **animated GIF** becomes a sprite sheet with its frames' delays (WE's `TEXS0003` frame table), several images can be imported **as an image sequence** with a frame duration, and an **MP4** becomes a video image layer (WE 2.2), its movie in a video `.tex`.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Add Layer: Light, Model, Camera, Full Composition Layer, Solid Placeholder and Preset**, the rest of Wallpaper Engine's Add Asset dialog. **Light** adds WE's new light (a point light of radius 500 and intensity 10 at the view's centre, raised to z 250, in a 2D scene; radius 5 and intensity 5 in a 3D one), or a spot, tube or directional light at once. **Model…** lists the wallpaper's 3D models (`.mdl`) and WE's and adds a model layer. **Camera** adds a camera layer framing what the scene's camera frames, so the view doesn't move. **Full Composition Layer** (2D scenes) covers the whole wallpaper with what was drawn before it (`models/util/projectlayer.json`), and **Solid Placeholder** is WE's replaceable solid layer (an instanced solid model kept with the edits, white, 256 × 256). **Preset…** offers WE's presets that add other layers than particle systems, read from your copy of WE's assets: Clock and 3D Clock, Countdown and the Light Shafts shapes (their built-in effect copied into the project as an added effect's); each variant is one undo step.
- **Scene gravity and wind are read.** A scene's Physics options (`gravitydirection`, `gravitystrength`, `windenabled`, `winddirection`, `windstrength`, bindable to user properties) are decoded with Wallpaper Engine's defaults, and the wind is Wallpaper Engine's own: simplex noise over time and the point's place across the scene, never blowing against its direction. In Wallpaper Engine only Puppet Warp's rope simulation uses them (bone springs and models keep their own gravity), so nothing draws differently yet; no library wallpaper has a rope. See docs/models-plan.md §2.14.
- **Scene `clearenabled`**, as in Wallpaper Engine. A scene whose `general.clearenabled` is false, or whose script sets `thisScene.clearenabled = false`, no longer has its frame cleared before it draws: like Wallpaper Engine, which skips its scene pass's clear (colour and depth) then, each frame draws over the last, so moving layers leave trails. It is on by default, as before.
- **On battery: use a lower quality preset** (Settings › Performance › Playback, off by default). While the Mac runs on battery or in Low Power Mode, wallpapers draw with a Low, Medium (the default) or High preset, or Keep My Settings, and an optional 15, 20 or 30 FPS cap. It only lowers: a setting you have lower stays as you set it. It is an overlay, so nothing is saved, the Preset control still shows your choice, and your own settings come back on power. It switches live, from the power-source and Low Power Mode notifications, without reloading the wallpaper (a change of anti-aliasing, post-processing or shadows rebuilds the scene's content in place). On a 4K display, against Ultra at 60 fps, the battery Medium preset at 30 fps cut the GPU time per second by about 70 % on a bloom scene (5.2 → 3.1 ms a frame) and 57 % on a 37-layer particle scene (8.7 → 7.4 ms a frame); from the default Medium settings the Low preset cut it by about 66 %. The Wallpaper Editor keeps drawing at your own settings. Wallpaper Engine's own **Laptop on battery** rule (Keep Running, Pause, Stop) is now listed only on Macs with a battery, as Wallpaper Engine lists it only on laptops.
- **Wallpaper Engine's command line.** The app's executable takes WE's `-control` commands and hands them to the running app: `pause`, `stop`, `play`, `mute`, `unmute`, `openWallpaper` (on a display by `-monitor` or `-location`, with a `-preset`, or in a window with `-playInWindow`, `-width`, `-height`, `-x`, `-y`, `borderless` and `activate`), `nextWallpaper`, `closeWallpaper`, `openPlaylist`, `openProfile`, `applyProperties` (`RAW~(…)~END` JSON), `hideIcons`, `showIcons` and `getWallpaper`, which prints the wallpaper's `project.json`. WE's spellings work as they are, and so does this app's launch-argument style (`--control open-wallpaper --file … --play-in-window …`). See docs/command-line.md.
- **Play in Window**, as Wallpaper Engine's: a wallpaper's context menu plays it in an ordinary, resizable window beside the desktop, as a **Full HD Preview** (1920 × 1080 pixels), a **Phone Preview** (WE's 607 × 1080) or a **Maximized Preview**, shrunk to fit the screen when needed. Every wallpaper type the app plays works there, on a renderer of its own, at the desktop's volume and speed; the window takes the mouse and keyboard (a scene sees the cursor and clicks over it, a web page gets them directly) and can go full screen. Choosing another wallpaper shows it in the same window, as WE reuses its "Wallpaper Pop-out" window. A web wallpaper plays in a window once it has been trusted as a wallpaper.
- **Hotkeys for wallpapers and display profiles**, as Wallpaper Engine's. A wallpaper's context menu has **Assign Hotkey…**: the shortcut, pressed in any app, sets that wallpaper on the display that was selected when it was assigned (found again by the display's identity after reconnecting). Once assigned, the menu shows **Hotkey: ⌃⌥1** with Change Hotkey… and Remove Hotkey. The Displays sheet's Profile menu has **Hotkeys**, listing each profile with its hotkey; choosing one assigns, changes or removes it, and a deleted profile's hotkey goes with it. A shortcut that a playlist, a hotkey action, another wallpaper or profile, a menu command, macOS or another app uses asks first and names it, as the other hotkeys do. Settings › General › Hotkeys lists them in WE's **Change Wallpaper** group, with a Remove button each. A wallpaper that runs code still asks for trust the first time.
- **Video loading: From disk or In memory** (Settings › Optimizations › Video), Wallpaper Engine's `videoreadmode`. From disk (the default) is as before. AVFoundation reads a video past the system's file cache, so a looping video reads its whole file from the disk again on every loop: a 137 MB 4K video with a 27.6 s loop read 143 MB per loop, about 5 MB/s for as long as it plays. In memory reads the file once and plays it from memory, so nothing more is read from the disk (a hard disk can sleep, a network volume stays quiet), for about the file's size in memory (215 MB against 18 MB for that video). It applies to video wallpapers on both the AVKit and the Metal path, from the next time a video opens.
- **Media blocklist** (Settings › Optimizations › Audio, below Media integration support), Wallpaper Engine's `mediablocklist`. It names the app of the current media session with a Block button and lists the blocked apps with Unblock. Wallpapers don't see what a blocked app plays (title, artist, album cover and its colours, timeline): to them nothing is playing until another app plays.
- **Audio recording device and Recording volume** (Settings › Optimizations › Audio), Wallpaper Engine's `audioinputdevice` and `audioinputvolume`. Audio-reactive wallpapers (scenes, SceneScript's audio buffers and web wallpapers' audio listeners) can hear a microphone or a loopback device such as BlackHole instead of the sound the Mac plays (Default). Choosing a device asks for the Microphone permission; while it isn't granted or the device is disconnected, the system audio is recorded, and a device that reconnects is recorded again. Recording volume (0 to 200, default 50 as in Wallpaper Engine) scales the spectrum: 100 doubles it. Both apply at once, without reloading the wallpapers.
- **Web wallpaper devtools**, Wallpaper Engine's *CEF devtools* (Settings › Advanced there): Settings › Optimizations › Developer Tools has *Web wallpaper devtools*, off by default and only for the session (it is never saved). On, WebKit pages become inspectable from Safari's Develop menu, and the Chromium engine opens Chromium's DevTools on this Mac only (127.0.0.1, port 9222, where chrome://inspect also finds it); Chromium pages reload once to pick it up. **Open Devtools** opens the page list on that port for Chromium wallpapers, or Safari for WebKit ones, and says "No web wallpaper active." without one ([docs/chromium-engine.md](docs/chromium-engine.md#devtools)).
- **Wallpapers' own translations** (project.json `general.localization`). Property titles, text rows and combo choices that a wallpaper writes as `ui_` keys now show the author's text in the app's language (the language scripts get through `applyGeneralSettings`), falling back to the author's English and then the key, as Wallpaper Engine resolves them; Wallpaper Engine's own translation of a key still wins. They show in Details, Scene Edit / Export, the Wallpaper Editor's property choices and the MCP property listing, without the markup authors put in titles.
- **User shortcuts** (Wallpaper Engine 2.7's `usershortcut` property). A shortcut row in Details shows what it's bound to; **Assign Shortcut** opens Wallpaper Engine's choices (Open File, Open Folder, Open Website, Run Command) with Test, Clear and Apply. Clicking the wallpaper's element (`engine.openUserShortcut`) opens the file in its default app, the folder in Finder, the website in your browser, or runs the command in zsh with your login environment, and returns true when it did. The binding is saved per wallpaper with its other properties, in Wallpaper Engine's form (`type:hash:path`), so one copied from another Mac stays blocked; the author's value, presets and Share JSON never bind one. Scripts get `{isbound, commandtype, file}` as wallpaper64.exe makes them.
- **Wallpaper Editor › Thumbnail: Take Snapshot and Record GIF**, as Wallpaper Engine's snapshot tool makes a wallpaper's preview. Take Snapshot draws the canvas's scene again offscreen and keeps its centre square (up to 1024 pixels) as `preview.jpg`; Record GIF draws it at one of Wallpaper Engine's six GIF formats (256×256 at 25 FPS for 2 seconds, 256×256 at 12 FPS for 4 seconds, 128×128 at 25 FPS for 8 seconds, dithered or not) into a looping `preview.gif` with one optimised palette, made 32 pixels smaller with 128 colours until it fits Steam's 1 MB, as Wallpaper Engine's encoder does. The result shows with Use and Discard. Save as New Wallpaper gives the new wallpaper the thumbnail in use (it used to copy the original's preview), and File › Save writes it into a wallpaper of your own; project.json's `preview` names it and the library shows it at once. Without one, the wallpaper keeps its own preview.
- **Copy to and Swap with in Display Settings**, as in Wallpaper Engine. Under *Wallpaper per display*, right-click a display (or a split region) to copy its wallpaper, with that wallpaper's properties and display options there, to another display, or to swap the two displays' wallpapers and settings. Displays in a clone or stretch group aren't offered.
- **Exact phrase and Hide Anime in the Workshop tab**, as in Wallpaper Engine. Once the search has two words, an *Exact phrase* checkbox by the search field sends it quoted, so Steam finds the words together and in order (a search you quote yourself is sent as typed). *Hide Anime*, in the filter sidebar's new Filter Settings section, leaves out the Anime, MMD, Girls, Guys and Music genres unless you tick one of them; it is saved, and Reset Filters keeps it.
- **Favorite and Last Updated sorts in Installed**, as in Wallpaper Engine. Favorite lists your favourites first, each part by name; Last Updated lists the most recently updated Workshop items first, by Steam's update time when the app has read it and otherwise by when the item's folder last changed, with local wallpapers last. The direction button reverses both.
- **Wallpaper Engine's Workshop sorts.** The Workshop tab sorts by Top Rated, Most Popular (Year), Most Popular (Month), Most Popular (Week), Most Popular (Today), Most Recent, Most Up Votes and Most Subscriptions, in Wallpaper Engine's order, and starts on Most Popular (Year) as Wallpaper Engine does. *Trending*, *Most Popular* and *Most Subscribed* are gone: Most Popular is now Top Rated, and Trending, which had no time window, is one of the Most Popular sorts.
- **Web wallpapers' folder properties work**, Wallpaper Engine's `directory` user property, so slideshow web wallpapers show your pictures. Choose a folder in the wallpaper's properties: with `fetchall`, the page gets every matching file in it and its subfolders through `wallpaperPropertyListener.userDirectoryFilesAddedOrChanged`, then each file added or changed and `userDirectoryFilesRemoved` for each one deleted, as the folder changes (FSEvents); with `ondemand`, `wallpaperRequestRandomFileForProperty` answers with a random file. Only Wallpaper Engine's file types count: images (`.png`, `.apng`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.bmp`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`) or, for a video folder, `.webm` and `.ogv`. Pages open these files, and a `file` property's file, as Wallpaper Engine documents (`'file:///' + path`) in WebKit and Chromium alike; only the chosen file and the matching files of the chosen folders can be read, nothing else outside the wallpaper.
- **Settings › General › Screen Saver Same as Wallpaper** (on by default, below Show Wallpaper on Lock Screen): on, each display's screen saver shows that display's own wallpaper. It is read from what is set as the screen saver, so Set as Screen Saver (a menu, the Details panel, the Screen Saver tab or MCP) turns it off, turning it on clears what was set, and turning it off sets the main display's wallpaper as the screen saver. Restore Defaults and Reset Config turn it back on; MCP's `screensaver_get` reports it as `same_as_wallpaper`.
- **Caches clean up after themselves, and Settings › Performance can clear them.** Optimised textures, loading snapshots, editor previews, scene video textures and repaired videos unused for 60 days are deleted a while after launch and then daily in the background; what the wallpapers on screen use is always kept, and a deleted wallpaper's repaired videos go with it. The new *Caches* section shows how much space the caches take (macOS's GPU shader cache for the app included) and has **Clear Caches…**, which deletes them except what is in use; wallpapers load slower once afterwards, and the GPU shader cache is cleared the next time the app starts. MCP has `caches_get` and `caches_clear`. Scene video textures moved from `~/Library/Caches/VideoTextures` into the app's own caches folder; the old folder empties as its files expire.
- **The screen saver is live, and nothing is recorded any more.** While the screen saver runs, Open Wallpaper Engine draws each display's wallpaper live, as the screen saver's layout plans it, so clocks, dates, scripts and audio-reactive parts move as on the desktop; the screen saver shows each frame as it is drawn. Web wallpapers and WebM videos are drawn by the Chromium engine (WebKit stops a page the screen saver covers): without it they show their picture, and Settings › Plugins › Screen Saver offers to install it. Video wallpapers play their own file. Until the first frames come, each display shows its lock-screen picture, and when the app isn't running the screen saver launches it in the background, with no window or Dock icon. Scene Edit / Export's Screen Saver tab's **Set as Screen Saver** makes the chosen wallpaper the screen saver, drawn live with the tab's layer and property choices. The loop recordings, Record and Set as Screen Saver, Preview Recording and the daily re-recording are gone; a recording you had set as the screen saver becomes that wallpaper drawn live, and the old recordings are deleted. MCP's `screensaver_set` replaces `screensaver_record` and the schedule tools. Two screen savers show it: the classic one, and a newer screen saver extension inside the app. A background item (System Settings › General › Login Items) starts the app for them; if you turn it off there, Settings › Plugins › Screen Saver says so. Turning the Screen Saver plugin off keeps the pictures it shows first ([docs/screen-saver.md](docs/screen-saver.md)).
- **Choose whether the app shows in the Dock and the menu bar.** Settings › General › macOS has *Show in Dock* (keeps the icon while no window is open; off, it shows only while a window is open, as before) and *Show in Menu Bar*. With both off, the app keeps running in the background once its windows close; open it again from Applications or Spotlight to show its window.
- **Select All (⌘A) in the Installed tab** selects every wallpaper the folder shown lists, after the search and filters, as Finder does; from Edit › Select All too. In the search box or a name prompt, ⌘A still selects the text.
- **Drops into a folder animate.** The moved tiles shrink and fade out while the grid closes up, and the folder tile or breadcrumb pops once; with Reduce Motion they only fade and the folder only flashes. Dragging several wallpapers shows a stack of up to three of them with a count, as Finder and Photos do.
- **Create Folder in a wallpaper's context menu**, as Finder's New Folder with Selection: it makes a folder in the folder shown, named *New Folder* (numbered when that name is taken), moves the wallpaper (or the selection it is in) into it, and asks for the folder's name.
- **Folders in the Installed tab, as Wallpaper Engine has them.** Create folders (nested if you like) from the grid's context menu or the bottom bar, rename them, give them one of Wallpaper Engine's icons and colours, and remove them (their wallpapers go back to the top level; nothing is deleted). Folders show first in the grid and open with a click, with breadcrumbs back. Move wallpapers, or the selection, by dragging them onto a folder or a breadcrumb, or with *Move to Folder* in their menu; a wallpaper is in one folder at most. Search and filters apply within the folder shown, as in Wallpaper Engine. Folders are saved by the same keys as favourites, so a Workshop wallpaper downloaded again is back in its folder, and they go with *Export Settings…*. When the Wallpaper Engine folder chosen for the assets has folders in its `config.json`, the setup assistant and Settings › Assets ask *Also import your Wallpaper Engine folders?*; they merge into yours, and importing again adds nothing. The MCP server lists them (`folders_list`), creates them (`folder_create`) and files wallpapers in them (`wallpaper_move_to_folder`) ([docs/features.md](docs/features.md)).
- **Import Wallpaper Engine's favourites.** Wallpaper Engine keeps its favourites in your Steam account (your Workshop favourites), so once the assets are installed or a Wallpaper Engine folder is chosen, the setup assistant and Settings › Assets ask *Also import your Wallpaper Engine favourites?* when Steam lists any that aren't in My Favourites yet, and show how many were added. Your current favourites stay, and importing again adds only new ones. It uses your Steam Web API key and the account Steam's own files name (the SteamCMD login, or the last login of the Steam folder the chosen install is in); without them nothing is offered. *Import Wallpaper Engine Favourites…* in Settings › Assets checks again ([docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md#wallpaper-engine-favourites)).

### Changed

- **Video wallpapers play live in the screen saver, drawn by the app like scenes and web pages.** No file is linked or copied into the screen saver's folder any more. When the desktop already plays the video on a display, the screen saver draws from that player (or, on the Metal video path, from its running scene), so the video is decoded once; otherwise the app opens a player of its own. Each frame is drawn once, at the video's own frame rate, in the desktop's placement, and never larger than the placed video (the saver scales it up). Stretch, clone and split layouts work as for scenes. A video set as the screen saver starts on its first frame. When the app starts, the video files earlier versions linked or copied into the screen saver's folder are deleted (only its own, named as it named them; nothing in the library), and a video an earlier version set as the screen saver is drawn live.
- **Shaders are translated through one front end.** The text pass that paired a shader's vertex and fragment stages by matching lines (`ShaderPairRewriter`) is gone: its rules (varyings matched by name, writable inputs, attribute locations, texture bindings, stage-local uniforms) are now part of the HLSL front end and work on the shader's tokens, for effects, materials, models, puppets and particles alike. GLSL reserved words a shader uses as names (`common`, `input`, `sample`, …) get their own names back in the compiled shader, so its constants carry Wallpaper Engine's names without a lookup table. Shaders translate again once after updating.
- **Set as Screen Saver sets the wallpaper at once and takes web wallpapers.** In the Installed, Discover and Workshop menus it no longer opens Scene Edit / Export: the wallpaper becomes the screen saver with its default settings (every layer and clock on), and customising it stays in the Screen Saver tab. Web wallpapers and WebM videos can be set too, drawn live through the Chromium engine; without the engine, choosing it offers the install. The Details panel's *Screen Saver Available* row is now a **Set as Screen Saver** button below **Set as Wallpaper** (renamed from *Set Wallpaper*): disabled with the reason where it can't apply, and a checked **Screen Saver** with **Stop Using as Screen Saver** beside it when the wallpaper is the screen saver. MCP's `screensaver_set` takes web wallpapers as well.
- **The Downloads and Playlists tabs are redesigned**, as Safari and the App Store list downloads and Music and Photos show playlists. Downloads are grouped into In Progress, Queued, Failed and Completed, each with a count; a row shows the preview, the author, Workshop ID and size, and while steamcmd reports a percentage, the speed and the time left. A failed row shows steamcmd's message and a Retry button; a finished one has Set as Wallpaper and Show in Finder on hover and in its menu; the toolbar has *Retry All Failed* and *Clear Completed*, and a notice says when SteamCMD isn't set up or logged in. Each playlist in the sidebar has a cover made from its first four wallpapers, its count and a mark on the one playing. Its page has a large cover, the name (click to rename), the count, how long a round takes, its timing and transition, and Play, Shuffle, Previous, Next and Configure; its wallpapers show as a grid (or a list) with their type and how long each shows, drag to reorder, and have Set as Wallpaper, Show in Installed, Move Up, Move Down and Remove in their menu. *Create Playlist* on the empty tab starts a playlist with its name ready to edit.
- **Workshop downloads after the first start right away.** SteamCMD stays running and logged in between downloads instead of starting and logging in again for each one, so queued downloads run back to back; it quits after five idle minutes, when the login changes, before other SteamCMD work and when the app quits. If it stops answering or loses its connection, the item gets one more try in a new SteamCMD. With three small items that was about 13 s before and 6 s after; previews and logging in still start SteamCMD on their own.
- **A cloned or stretched web wallpaper runs once in the Chromium web engine.** On a clone the page (or WebM video) loads on the main clone display and the other displays show it, as Wallpaper Engine mirrors a clone; on a stretch it is laid out once on the whole canvas and each display shows its part. The pointer and clicks on any display reach the page and its sound plays once. On two displays that is about 40 % less CPU and GPU and 130 to 380 MB less memory. WebKit still loads a page per display.
- **Texture Resolution's High Performance also draws web wallpapers at half resolution**, as Wallpaper Engine starts its web renderer with `-halfresolution` for that setting (and only for it), in WebKit and in Chromium. With *Render web wallpapers at standard resolution* also on, whichever draws fewer pixels wins. On a test page with CSS animations and a canvas on a 1080p display, the page's GPU time fell by about 18% in both engines, and its memory by about 50 MB in WebKit and 120 MB in Chromium.
- **The README, the docs, the website and the wiki describe this release.** The privacy policy (in the app, in docs/legal and on the website) now lists the **Microphone** permission, which the app asks for only when you choose a recording device in Settings › Optimizations › Audio; audio from it is analysed on your Mac and never recorded or sent.
- **Demo clips in the README and the wiki**: short looping clips of setting a wallpaper, scenes running live, Scene Edit / Export, the Wallpaper Editor, Live Photo and Android export, and Play in Window ([docs/media/demo](docs/media/demo/README.md)).

### Fixed

- **Wallpaper previews and test builds no longer ask for the microphone either.** The looping video previews in the app's windows played on the default output device, so with a headset that also records macOS asked for Microphone access. They now play on the same output-only device as the wallpapers. So do the video players in the unit tests, which made every new local test build ask again.
- **Stopping the screen saver or a video no longer crashes the app now and then.** A video frame still on the GPU when its player stopped (the live screen saver ending, or a scene's video texture or a video wallpaper on the Metal path being torn down) was let go after the texture cache that made it, and handing it back wrote into freed memory (EXC_BAD_ACCESS). Each frame in flight now keeps its texture cache until it's done.
- **Playing a wallpaper no longer asks for the microphone.** With a headset or another output device that also records, macOS asked for Microphone access as soon as a scene's sound layers or a video wallpaper's sound started, although no recording device was chosen. While the prompt was open, the wallpaper's render thread waited for it, and the next wallpaper change logged "did not stop within 5 s". Wallpaper sound now plays on the output device without its inputs: a private output-only (stacked) device that follows the default output device. The scene sound engine no longer opens the hardware itself, and starting or stopping its output never runs on the render thread. The Microphone permission is now asked for only when you choose a recording device in Settings › Optimizations › Audio.
- **Wallpaper folders that are symbolic links work.** In a library made of links to wallpaper folders elsewhere, every listing of a wallpaper's files failed, because Foundation doesn't follow a link a listing starts from. Scenes logged "Loading snapshot: can't read <id>" and never got a loading snapshot, so the desktop showed the Workshop preview while they loaded. Their sounds weren't found for the Details panel and their size read 0. A linked wallpaper (or linked dependency, or linked library folder) now runs from the folder the link points to. Deleting a linked wallpaper removes only the link.
- **Exporting no longer makes the watchdog stop the desktop's wallpaper.** Scene Edit / Export's iPhone & iPad and Android previews (and the Screen Saver preview) run a private copy of the scene, framed for the export, whose frames are slow while it draws a phone-sized crop at full detail. Their frame times went to the render watchdog with the desktop's, so after a few export previews it stopped the wallpaper on the desktop with "made Open Wallpaper Engine unresponsive" although the desktop drew in time. Only a copy a display can run reports to the watchdog now; a real hang still trips its main-thread check.
- **Videos imported in the Wallpaper Editor are video textures again, in Wallpaper Engine's layout.** The editor wrote an MP4's `.tex` with the old guess at the `TEXB0004` header (an "is video" word), which the texture-variant reader now reads as a variant count, so it found no movie. It now writes what Wallpaper Engine writes (format 0, the Clamp UVs and video flags, FreeImage format -1, no variants, the MP4 as the one mipmap), and a `.tex` is read as a video from that flag, so Wallpaper Engine's own video textures are recognised as videos too.
- **Effects can read the layer's matrix, `g_LayerModelMatrix`.** Wallpaper Engine's shader variable for transforming between a layer's local space and world space was missing, so a shader that declared it read zeros. Workshop effects use it to read the layer's scale back (the rounded mask effect in 3651835769 uses it to correct for the layer's scale). It is the layer's own transform with its parents', and an effect that reads it redraws when the layer is moved, turned or rescaled.
- **Effect conditions in Wallpaper Engine 2.x's comparison form work.** An effect's passes, texture binds and buffers can be conditional on a combo compared with `ge`, `gt`, `le` or `lt` (`{"POINTEMITTER": {"op": "ge", "value": 2}}`), as well as equal to a value; only the equal form decoded before, and a comparison dropped the whole condition. Bind and buffer conditions are now honoured too: a bind whose condition fails leaves the slot to the material's texture, and a buffer whose condition no pass meets isn't made, so the Fluid Simulation effect no longer allocates its lighting normal map with lighting off.
- **SceneScript `IEffect.executeMaterialFunction(name)` runs the effect's functions.** It used to do nothing and log "not supported yet". It now runs the effect.json `functions` entry it names, as Wallpaper Engine does: a `clear` sets that entry's FBOs back to their start colour before the effect's next frame, so a script can reset the Fluid Simulation effect's flow (`clearVelocity`) or its dye (`clearDye`). A name the effect doesn't have, or an action Wallpaper Engine doesn't have, is logged once.
- **Particles collide with Puppet Warp images.** A `collisionmodel` operator linked to a puppet image logged that it isn't a model and collided with nothing; Wallpaper Engine reads the image's rig as a model's, and the particles now collide with a capsule per bone, posed as the image's animation layers move it (or with the rig's box when it has no per-bone boxes).
- **Child particle systems keep their links' depth in 3D scenes.** A `children` link's `origin.z`, `scale.z` and `angles.x` / `angles.y` were dropped; Wallpaper Engine builds each link's full 3D matrix, and the app now draws a child through it in a perspective scene (an event child's instances keep the depth offset and scale; their turn out of the plane shows as the tilted emitter's, as a tilted layer's does in an orthographic scene).
- **A particle control point that copies its parent's can take its raw value**, Wallpaper Engine's control-point flag 8: the parent system's point is copied as it is in the parent's space instead of being carried into the child's. A point with both "copy from parent" and "worldspace" now copies from the parent, as Wallpaper Engine checks the parent first. Control points' `angles` stay unread, as in Wallpaper Engine, which parses them but never applies them (only the object's control point angle overrides turn a point).
- **Particle colour lists keep every colour.** A `colorlist` initializer kept only its first four colours and logged the rest; Wallpaper Engine keeps the whole list (its editor offers up to ten) and picks among all of them, and so does the app now, on the GPU and the CPU alike.
- **SceneScript cursor events reach 3D models**, as Wallpaper Engine 2.x's "hitboxes and click events to models": `cursorEnter`, `cursorLeave`, `cursorMove`, `cursorDown`, `cursorUp` and `cursorClick` now fire on a model layer's scripts, hit tested as `wallpaper64.exe` does, against the model's box through its world matrix (including WE's own placement of that box, which spans 0 to the model's size from its origin), with `localPosition` where the cursor's ray enters it. In perspective scenes the cursor is now a ray from the camera's eye, so image and text layers placed in 3D are hit where they are drawn, and the objects are tried nearest first, Wallpaper Engine's 3D click sorting; `solid` and `disablepropagation` apply to models as to images.
- **`CursorEvent.hitBox`** (Wallpaper Engine 2.x's named hit boxes on puppet warp layers and models): when a rig's `.mdl` has per-bone hit boxes, a click, release or drag over one names its bone in the event, the topmost limb of a puppet or the nearest box of a model, and a model's event reports where the cursor's ray enters that box. Hover events don't carry it, as in Wallpaper Engine. Puppets are still hit through their image's rectangle, as Wallpaper Engine tests them.
- **3D models draw every pass of their material.** A model material with several passes now draws each one in the material's order, over what the one before drew, with that pass's own shader, textures, constants, blending and depth and cull state, as Wallpaper Engine draws a material's passes. Before, only the first pass drew. A later pass that can't be made is logged and left out.
- **Fur on 3D models.** A model material through Wallpaper Engine's `fur4` shader draws every fur shell: each mesh is drawn as many times as its *Fur quality* (`INSTANCECOUNT`: 5, 9, 13 or 21) in one instanced draw, each instance pushed further out along the normals, as `fur4.vert` reads `gl_InstanceID`. Before, only the innermost shell (the bare mesh) drew. The same holds for any model shader that declares an `INSTANCECOUNT` combo.
- **Scripts that change a text layer's layout are drawn.** Writes to `font`, `anchor`, `padding`, `maxwidth` / `limitwidth` and `maxrows` / `limitrows` (`thisLayer.maxwidth = …`, or a script bound to the field) used to be stored and ignored; the text is laid out again with them the frame they land, as Wallpaper Engine lays a text object out again when one of its fields changes. A font a script names is loaded from the wallpaper, WE's assets or Workshop items on first use. A layout field bound to a script or a user property (`"maxwidth": {"script": …, "value": 1200}`) also kept no value at all, so the text didn't wrap until the script ran; it now starts at the authored value. Katana Girl (3238423642) wraps its Artist Name and Song Title at the width its scripts compute.
- **Scripts' `alignment`, `perspective`, `rootmotion` and camera `zoom` are drawn.** SceneScript could set `IImageLayer.alignment`, `IEffectLayer.perspective`, `IModelLayer.perspective` and `rootmotion`, and `ICamera.zoom`, and read them back, but the renderer kept the authored values. A layer now draws about the alignment a script set; a layer or model whose script turns `perspective` on draws through Wallpaper Engine's temporary perspective camera in a 2D scene (an authored `perspective` model now does too, as in Wallpaper Engine); switching `rootmotion` takes effect from the next frame; and a camera layer's scripted zoom zooms a 2D scene, a playing camera path's zoom still taking precedence.
- **SceneScript's `engine.isRunningInEditor()` is true in the Wallpaper Editor.** Wallpaper Engine's editor tells scripts they run there ("whether the script is currently running inside the editor"), and scripts use it to show helpers only while authoring. The Wallpaper Editor's canvas now returns true; the displays, the screen saver and Scene Edit / Export, which aren't the editor, still return false.
- **SceneScript video textures no longer carry a stray `getAnimation`.** `IVideoTexture` had a copy of the animation layer's `getAnimation`, which called a missing helper and threw a TypeError. Wallpaper Engine's typings give a video texture no `getAnimation` (it isn't an `IObject`), so it is gone, as in Wallpaper Engine.
- **The library fits its window while the Wallpaper Engine assets are missing.** The "Scenes need Wallpaper Engine assets" banner sized its line to its full wrapped height, and when the split view measured the column narrow, that height pushed the grid and the Create Playlist, Create Folder and Edit Wallpaper buttons past the bottom of the window (and the Details title past its top) at the smallest window size, 1000 × 692. The line now wraps to at most two lines, and everything fits.
- **Opening Scene Edit / Export no longer sends AppKit into a layout loop.** The first time it opened, in any mode, AppKit laid the window out 300 times and logged `-layoutSubtreeIfNeeded … continued for 300 iterations`: the object list's search was attached to the whole split view, so its place in the toolbar and the columns' widths kept re-laying each other out next to the right-hand panel. The search is now on the object list's column, where it shows, and the window lays out in a few passes.
- **Test runs and isolated copies never touch the keychain.** A test host reading the steamcmd account name waited on a macOS keychain prompt, and a full local test run sat idle for over half an hour. A copy started with `OWE_ISOLATED_STATE` (and every test host) now keeps its Steam Web API key and steamcmd account name in memory for as long as it runs; the app itself keeps them in the keychain as before.
- **Web wallpapers get a dropdown's value with the type its author gave it**, as Wallpaper Engine passes it: an option authored as `"value": 3` reaches `applyUserProperties` as the number 3 (and a string, decimal or true/false option as that type), the user's choice included. Pages that compare strictly (`case 3:`, `=== 2`) now see the choice; Customizable Module Visualizer Web (1081733658) switched to its slideshow background only this way. Scenes' scripts already got typed values.
- **macOS's GPU shader cache no longer fills up.** Metal keeps compiled shaders per app in a cache whose usage database holds 1 MB; once full, it logged "MDB_MAP_FULL: Environment mapsize limit reached" and stopped recording. The app now clears that cache at launch when its shaders changed (a new shader translator or pipeline archive revision) or the database is full, but only while no other copy of the app uses it. Test runs and development copies started with `OWE_ISOLATED_STATE` keep their Metal cache (and temporary folder) apart from the app's, so they no longer fill the user's.
- **System Settings › Wallpaper shows the lock-screen picture at once.** Its preview stayed black, or showed an older picture, until another display was chosen: OWE alternated two names per display, and macOS's wallpaper agent, which caches pictures by URL and size, kept a picture it read while OWE was writing over that name. Each picture now gets a new name, is written in full before it is set, and the newest four per display stay for other Spaces.
- **System Settings' screen saver preview shows the current still and updates.** It kept the still it found when the pane made it, so a new wallpaper or pick showed only after reopening the pane, and a view could end on another display's still. The savers now watch their folder and show a new still at once (the newest asked for wins), and the preview runs while it has a window, showing live frames whenever the app draws them.
- **Live Photos from iPhone & iPad Export move on the Lock Screen.** iOS 17 and later took them as Live Photos but said "Motion Not Available: Motion from this Live Photo is not supported as a wallpaper."
